scope: General harness design, auditing, and improvement for agentic software development; no project-specific implementation requirements.

sources.title: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
sources.annotation: Targeted editing, search, and feedback tools improve the evaluated SWE setup. Model and benchmark versions limit transfer.

sources.title: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-based Software Engineering Agents
sources.annotation: Localization, repair, and validation form a bounded pipeline; counterevidence to the assumption that greater agent autonomy necessarily helps.

sources.title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
sources.annotation: Real issue-to-patch tasks with test oracles. Existing tests define observed success, not a complete software specification.

sources.title: SWE-Search: Enhancing Software Agents with Monte Carlo Tree Search and Iterative Refinement
sources.annotation: Structured search can improve repairs; additional compute and value estimators are part of the method, not a free increase in determinism.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
sources.annotation: Interleaves reasoning, tool actions, and observations. An execution pattern without technical enforcement of permissions.

sources.title: Reflexion: Language Agents with Verbal Reinforcement Learning
sources.annotation: Verbal feedback is retained for later attempts. Success depends on feedback quality and task characteristics.

sources.title: Self-Refine: Iterative Refinement with Self-Feedback
sources.annotation: Iterative feedback from the same model. An improvement hypothesis, not independent evidence of correctness.

sources.title: Large Language Models Cannot Self-Correct Reasoning Yet
sources.annotation: Intrinsic correction without external feedback can fail on the evaluated reasoning tasks. No universal verdict on newer models.

sources.title: CRITIC: Large Language Models Can Self-Correct with Tool-Interactive Critiquing
sources.annotation: Tool observations support correction. Together with P08, relevant to separating critique from a checkable oracle.

sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
sources.annotation: Evaluates tool/user interaction and policies; pass^k measures repeated success. Service domains transfer only partly to software development.

sources.title: τ²-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
sources.annotation: Users and agents change the environment. Helps examine collaboration and state changes separately from answer quality.

sources.title: AppWorld: A Controllable World of Apps and People for Benchmarking Interactive Coding Agents
sources.annotation: Controlled application environment with functional and side-effect checks. Success also needs limits on unintended changes.

sources.title: OSWorld: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents for Open-Ended Tasks in Real Computer Environments
sources.annotation: Real desktop environments with assessable final states. Relevant to agents performing browser/GUI tasks.

sources.title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
sources.annotation: Reproducible web tasks with functional assessment. Website state and infrastructure belong to the experimental setup.

sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
sources.annotation: Tasks and attacks involving tool content provide a pattern for adversarial harness tests. No evidence of comprehensive defense.

sources.title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
sources.annotation: Attacks through external tool data. A transferable failure pattern for tickets, repository text, and logs.

sources.title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
sources.annotation: Separates control and untrusted data through capabilities and dataflow rules. Guarantees apply to the defined model; remaining limits matter.

sources.title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
sources.annotation: Trained prioritization of privileged instructions. Results do not establish an equivalent guarantee from additional prompt headings.

sources.title: StruQ: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Structured Queries
sources.annotation: Separate channels plus specific training. Delimiters alone in an unchanged model are not the same intervention.

sources.title: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
sources.annotation: Automatically checkable response conditions. Useful partial oracles with limited coverage of lifecycle rules and functional quality.

sources.title: Generalizing Verifiable Instruction Following
sources.annotation: New verifiable conditions examine overfitting to known instruction tests. Supports separating development and holdout cases.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
sources.annotation: Position-dependent use of long context in evaluated models. No universal maximum token count for current harnesses.

sources.title: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
sources.annotation: Declarative modules and metric-based optimization. Metric quality and holdouts remain decisive.

sources.title: Prompting Is Programming: A Query Language for Large Language Models
sources.annotation: Programmatic control and output conditions. Deterministic program logic does not automatically make linguistic meaning correct.

sources.title: JSONSchemaBench: A Rigorous Benchmark of Structured Outputs for Language Models
sources.annotation: Examines schema coverage, efficiency, and content quality. JSON conformance is a partial objective; engines cover schemas differently.

sources.title: ProbGuard: Proactive Runtime Monitoring for LLM Agent Safety via Probabilistic Prediction
sources.annotation: Learned probabilistic model for proactive monitoring. Risk thresholds are statistical decisions, not deterministic knowledge of future failures.

sources.title: Terminal-Bench: Benchmarking Agents on Hard, Realistic Tasks in Command Line Interfaces
sources.annotation: Version 2.0 includes 89 tasks with solutions and tests. Relevant to build, repair, and toolchain work.

sources.title: What Makes a Terminal-Bench Task Hard? Separating Genuine Hardness from Fake-Hardness on an Adjudicated Agentic Corpus
sources.annotation: Distinguishes genuine difficulty from faulty oracles, infrastructure problems, and bypass cases. Recent preprint; detailed methods were not inspected.

sources.title: MTAC-IFBench: Benchmarking Instruction-Following in Multi-Turn Agentic Coding
sources.annotation: Coding tasks with accumulated conditions. Evaluation uses judges as well as scripts; authors discuss judge bias and cost.

sources.title: Harness-Bench: Measuring Harness Effects across Models in Realistic Agent Workflows
sources.annotation: 106 tasks in the inspected paper version. Compares complete model/harness configurations; does not automatically isolate causal component effects.

sources.title: Agent Behavioral Contracts: Formal Specification and Runtime Enforcement for Reliable Autonomous AI Agents
sources.annotation: Exploratory contract architecture and its own evaluation. Abstract only; no basis for effectiveness promises or mandatory migration.

sources.title: Proof of Execution: Runtime Verification for Governed AI Agent Actions
sources.source_date: 2026-04-26 as reported on the page; metadata anomaly
sources.annotation: Binds executed steps to contracts under deployment assumptions. Abstract inspected; date and month identifier conflict. Supplementary reading, not central evidence.

sources.title: VIGIL: Runtime Enforcement of Behavioral Specifications in AI Agent Skills
sources.annotation: Historical artifact bindings plus SMT checks. Grounding and complete collection remain prerequisites; measured detection is imperfect.

sources.title: Getting Better at Working With You: Compiling User Corrections into Runtime Enforcement for Coding Agents
sources.annotation: Compiles corrections into rules and completion checks. Simulated users and recurring tasks limit transfer.

sources.title: Self-Healing Harness for Runtime Oversight of Agent Self-Modification
sources.annotation: Checks proposed changes against protected cases. Small experiments and missing comparison arms limit causal claims.

sources.title: AgentSpec: Customizable Runtime Enforcement for Safe and Reliable LLM Agents
sources.annotation: Triggers, conditions, and responses at action boundaries. Automatically generated rules and semantic predicates remain incomplete.

sources.title: Formal Policy Enforcement for Real-World Agentic Systems
sources.annotation: Versioned policy compiler and instrumented hosts. Formal guarantees require correct policies, observable facts, and complete mediation.

sources.title: Enforcing Temporal Constraints for LLM Agents
sources.annotation: Temporal constraints and controlled tool generation. Conformance of modeled traces is narrower than software's functional correctness.

sources.title: Breaking and Fixing Defenses Against Control-Flow Hijacking in Multi-Agent Systems
sources.annotation: Attacks and defenses using permitted call paths. Overly strict graphs can block necessary replanning; permitted paths can still carry harmful content.

sources.title: Constrained Decoding Eliminates Structural Failures in Small LLMs but Reveals a Scale-Dependent Semantic Gap
sources.annotation: Small recent study of small models. Supplementary counterevidence to equating schema success with content correctness.

sources.title: Decode-Time Grammars: Constrained LLM Generation over a Refinement Order of Grammar Fragments
sources.annotation: Generation over structured symbols and references. Narrow formal scope; only the abstract was assessed.

sources.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
sources.annotation: Observed failures in system design, coordination, and verification. Additional roles alone do not supply independent evidence.

sources.title: AI Agents That Matter
sources.annotation: Examines cost, reproducibility, and overfitting. Agent comparisons need traceable budgets and genuine test separation.

sources.title: Progent: Securing AI Agents with Privilege Control
sources.annotation: Symbolic tool permissions with checked narrowing or expansion. Initial policy and completeness of the tool boundary remain trust assumptions.

sources.title: Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents
sources.annotation: Executable code can outperform narrower action interfaces. Suitable sandboxes and mediated relevant external effects bound execution.

sources.title: Enforceable Security Policies
sources.annotation: Characterizes execution-monitor limits. Safety properties are narrower than arbitrary correctness, progress, or every information-flow requirement.

sources.title: The Protection of Information in Computer Systems
sources.annotation: Architectural principles for complete mediation, least privilege, and secure defaults. Foundational work, not an LLM effectiveness study.

sources.title: in-toto: Providing farm-to-table guarantees for bits and bytes
sources.annotation: Authenticated steps and artifact relationships. Integrity evidence does not prove complete tests or functionally correct results.

sources.title: Edit automata: enforcement mechanisms for run-time security policies
sources.annotation: Monitors can suppress or insert actions. Suitable formal rules and authority for replacement actions remain necessary.

sources.title: Solving a Million-Step LLM Task with Zero Errors
sources.annotation: MAKER combines predetermined decomposition, voting, and red flags on Hanoi. Correlated errors and open-ended software tasks limit transfer.

sources.title: The OpenHands Software Agent SDK: A Composable and Extensible Foundation for Production Agents
sources.annotation: State/event architecture with production evaluation. Bundled changes and excluded provider failures limit causal attribution.

sources.title: From Failed Trajectories to Reliable LLM Agents: Diagnosing and Repairing Harness Flaws
sources.annotation: HarnessFix connects traces, diagnosis, scoped repair operators, and regression checks with separate data splits. Local utility still needs measurement.

sources.title: MemoHarness: Agent Harnesses That Learn from Experience
sources.annotation: Experience bank and case-specific adaptation. Small primary test set, missing uncertainty intervals, and incomplete ablations limit claims.

sources.title: An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling
sources.annotation: A planner generates dependencies for controlled parallel execution. Incorrect planner references remain a separate failure source.

sources.title: ADaPT: As-Needed Decomposition and Planning with Language Models
sources.annotation: Recursive decomposition when execution struggles, with a depth limit. Model-based completion heuristics are not mandatory success evidence.

sources.title: Language Agent Tree Search Unifies Reasoning Acting and Planning in Language Models
sources.annotation: LATS combines search, model evaluations, and feedback. Additional compute and task selection are part of the intervention.

sources.title: Agent Workflow Memory
sources.annotation: Induced subroutines support offline and online web agents. Memory authorizes neither actions nor current completion.

sources.title: AutoCodeRover: Autonomous Program Improvement
sources.annotation: AST-based navigation and test-based fault localization for repair. Results depend on repositories and available tests.

sources.title: OpenHands: An Open Platform for AI Software Developers as Generalist Agents
sources.annotation: Platform for tool actions and software tasks. Distinct from the later SDK paper; background on runtime architecture.

sources.title: AgentCoder: Multi-Agent-based Code Generation with Iterative Testing and Optimisation
sources.annotation: Programmer, test-design, and execution roles for code-generation tasks. Role diversity does not prove verifier independence.

sources.title: MetaGPT: Meta Programming for A Multi-Agent Collaborative Framework
sources.annotation: Standardized workflows and intermediate artifacts organize collaboration. Prompt-based SOPs are not a complete runtime boundary.

sources.title: LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency
sources.annotation: Language tasks are formalized and processed by a classical planner. Validity depends on translation and the model.

sources.title: PlanBench: An Extensible Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models on Planning and Reasoning about Change
sources.annotation: Controlled planning tasks evaluate state changes. Historical model findings support no blanket claim about all current models.

sources.title: LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks
sources.annotation: Position paper combining proposals and external critics. Its title is not a universal empirical model assessment.

sources.title: Robust Planning with Compound LLM Architectures: An LLM-Modulo Approach
sources.annotation: Four scheduling domains with a verification loop. Correctness assumptions concern covered conditions and sound verifiers; successful search remains uncertain.

sources.title: Evaluating AGENTS.md: Are Repository-Level Context Files Helpful for Coding Agents?
sources.annotation: v3: CTXbench; no significant general gain over no context file; higher costs. Developer files outperform generated files.

sources.title: Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Software Tasks
sources.annotation: Time horizon refers to human expert time. A revision date does not automatically establish new model measurements.

sources.title: DSPy Assertions: Computational Constraints for Self-Refining Language Model Pipelines
sources.annotation: Hard and soft conditions control repair and stopping. Model-based predicates remain fallible.

sources.title: AgentOccam: A Simple Yet Strong Baseline for LLM-Based Web Agents
sources.annotation: Aligns observation and action spaces as a web-agent baseline. Competing hypothesis to indiscriminate increases in complexity.

sources.title: AFlow: Automating Agentic Workflow Generation
sources.annotation: Code-based workflow optimization with evaluation and repeated runs. Selected splits and benchmarks limit transfer.

sources.title: Debug like a Human: A Large Language Model Debugger via Verifying Runtime Execution Step-by-step
sources.annotation: LDB uses intermediate execution states for debugging. Model-based assessment of those states is not a formal proof.

sources.title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
sources.annotation: Additional inputs and differential testing expose overlooked errors. Reference solutions and input domains remain assumptions.

sources.title: Self-Consistency Improves Chain of Thought Reasoning in Language Models
sources.annotation: Aggregates multiple reasoning paths. Shared errors and task class limit majority reliability.

sources.title: Meta-Harness: End-to-End Optimization of Model Harnesses
sources.annotation: Code- and trace-based optimization. Terminal-Bench uses the same tasks for search and evaluation; mathematics has separate transfer assessment.

sources.title: Natural-Language Agent Harnesses
sources.annotation: Text describes policy; code implements exact mechanisms. Interpretation-dependent documents must be checked against executed behavior.

sources.title: Agent Systems with Harness Engineering: A Systematic Survey
sources.annotation: Survey of workflows, memory, and skills. Journal metadata and abstract inspected; full-text access remained limited.

sources.title: Agent Harness Engineering: A Survey
sources.annotation: Seven harness layers and mapping of public projects. Descriptive taxonomy bounded by publicly available information.

sources.title: From Question Answering to Task Completion: A Survey on Agent System and Harness Design
sources.annotation: Six coupled runtime responsibilities and task-dependent harness pressures. Orientation, not isolated effectiveness evidence.

sources.title: Harness Engineering for Language Agents: The Harness Layer as Control, Agency, and Runtime
sources.annotation: Non-peer-reviewed preprint with a conceptual decomposition and HarnessCard. Reporting proposal for models, control artifacts, and runtime policy.

sources.title: Harness engineering: leveraging Codex in an agent-first world
sources.annotation: Architecture checks, curated repository guidance, and a short entry map. Internal experience report, not a causal productivity study.

sources.title: Effective harnesses for long-running agents
sources.annotation: Initialization, feature lists, progress artifacts, and verifiable session completion. Engineering experience under concrete model/task assumptions.

sources.title: Harness design for long-running apps
sources.annotation: Planning, generation, and evaluation of longer application tasks. Reassess roles and criteria when models or tasks change.

sources.title: Demystifying evals for AI agents
sources.annotation: Separates tasks, trials, transcripts, graders, and outcomes. Useful methodology; independent evaluations remain necessary.

sources.title: Infrastructure noise
sources.annotation: Environment resources can affect agent scores. Capture resources, timeouts, and concurrency in run manifests.

sources.title: Building effective agents
sources.annotation: Distinguishes predefined workflows from model-directed agents. Simplicity is a starting choice, not a universal ranking.

sources.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents
sources.annotation: Task-appropriate context, retrieval, and compaction. Summaries do not replace authoritative workflow state.

sources.title: Writing effective tools for agents
sources.annotation: Tool names, arguments, and actionable feedback as design parameters. Measure improvement on real tasks.

sources.title: Managed agents
sources.annotation: Separates sessions, harnesses, models, and execution environments. Vendor architecture as experience, not a required platform.

sources.title: LangGraph: Persistence
sources.annotation: Checkpoints and persistent storage differ from RAM stores. Persistence needs a selected backend and retention contract.

sources.title: LangGraph: Interrupts
sources.annotation: Interrupted nodes restart on resume. Earlier effects need protection against repetition.

sources.title: Temporal Workflow Execution overview
sources.annotation: Workflow replay checks commands against recorded event history. Reconstruction is not identical fresh LLM generation.

sources.title: What is a Temporal Activity?
sources.annotation: Activities may be nondeterministic and retried after failure. External actions remain responsible for idempotency.

sources.title: Open Policy Agent: Introduction
sources.annotation: Separates policy decisions from enforcement. The calling effect path must actually respect the decision.

sources.title: What is Cedar?
sources.annotation: Authorization through principal, action, resource, and context. Schemas validate policies; runtime data needs a separate contract.

sources.title: SLSA Build: Provenance
sources.annotation: Verifiable relationships between builders, inputs, and outputs. Dependency completeness remains limited; provenance does not replace quality checks.
